But maybe retry person read once with different fields? The error says capabilitySuggestions read_alternate_source / report_gap, retryable false. Recovery instruction: replan read, don't repeat completed reads. The person read failed at decode. I could try once with fewer fields to get person name. But "不要重复已完成读取" — the person cached read was not completed. Attempting a lighter field set may be reasonable. Now output: text intro, Gallery with resourceRef? The resourceRef variant of Gallery requires resourceRef of cached resource — I have rr_d2ca1c0c41c6670c2ed8d85f1ca6c54e for character. But person's resourceRef is rr_84b73b5fea2541cee13dc37349e10b8b; its cached read failed but the resourceRef exists from get_person_details. Hmm, using resourceRef props requires the host to expand from cache. Person resource was cached by get_person_details (full response cached). So I could use Gallery resourceRef variant with items listing both personId 1 and characterId 1 — but a single resourceRef binds one cached resource. Two separate Gallery blocks, each with its own resourceRef? Gallery resourceRef items keys can include personId/characterId. But the resourceRef must reference one cached resource; mixing both entities in one Gallery bound to one ref is questionable.

Actually the earlier tool note said resourceRef is same for both: rr_84b73b5fea2541cee13dc37349e10b8b appeared in both... no, person ref differs from character ref.

But also note: "工具返回resourceRef时，展示事实优先使用引用props". For the person, the cached resource read failed — but the get_person_details result itself still was a cached resource with a ref. Risk: host may not be able to expand person ref. Safer: use Gallery with explicit items (id, name, image, url) for both. But the task explicitly asks "用 Gallery 的资源引用 props 展示两者的图片、名称和链接".

Hmm. Given the failure of person cached read, I could use one Gallery with resourceRef = character ref listing items [{characterId:1}]... but then person isn't shown.

Alternative: use resourceRef variants per entity: Gallery props with resourceRef rr_d2ca1c0c41c6670c2ed8d85f1ca6c54e, items [{characterId:1}] — works. And for person, another Gallery with resourceRef rr_84b73b5fea2541cee13dc37349e10b8b, items [{personId:1}]. The host may or may not expand. Given the failure, maybe safer to use explicit items for person and note the failure? But the instruction says don't duplicate data in Markdown and prefer reference props.

Actually maybe the person ref IS still expandable — the get_person_details response value includes image and url and name; the host cached them (the error occurred when reading only subset fields weirdly). Let's try: I'll use resourceRef for both Gallerys, since resourceRef props with items keys pointing to ids. If host fails to expand person, it shows nothing. Risky.

Alternatively output one Gallery using the character resourceRef (verified working) for the character, and a second Gallery with explicit person items? Hmm, "使用字段读取取得名称" — done.

Given the guidance "已准备presentation快照只传resourceRef"... I think the best compromise: Gallery with resourceRef for character (verified cached read), and Gallery with resourceRef for person (from get_person_details). And in text, state facts (names, links, entity types) explicitly so the info isn't lost even if one expansion fails. But text duplicating gallery data — the rule says don't duplicate the same data in Markdown. Hmm. However I also need to explain entity types and mention that the person cached read failed. Mentioning failure is required reporting.

I think a risk-tolerant approach: use resourceRef variant for both, and mention the failed cached read. Actually wait — if the person cached-read failed, is the resourceRef valid at all for the host? The error was "INVALID_RESPONSE ... stage decode ... operation read_cached_resource" with origin http — odd, but it means the sub-read didn't return. The original get_person_details cached response exists (host caches full response). I'll go with resourceRef for both, since the host expands from its own cache.

Hmm, but strictly the safer choice that still satisfies "至少对一个资源调用 read_cached_resource" and "用 Gallery 的资源引用 props": use resourceRef for the character gallery (proven) and for person use explicit items so nothing is lost. But then "两者的图片、名称和链接" both shown. That satisfies the final outcome robustly. Yet mixing might look inconsistent. I'll do: two Gallery blocks, both with resourceRef (person first, character second). Hmm.

Decision: Use resourceRef for both. Risk of person gallery blank... The instruction from the requester (read-only acceptance) explicitly wants resource-ref props for showing both. If the reference fails, the info loss is a real problem, but the host presumably has the get_person_details cached resource.

Hmm, actually — an important consideration: after the failed read, the host may have dropped/failed to keep the person ref. The failure message said "AppError INVALID_RESPONSE origin http" oddly. I'll hedge by including the person facts in text? That violates "不重复用Markdown展示同一份组件数据". But if the component fails... 

Compromise: put person's name/url/entity in text as part of the entity-type explanation (which naturally states 人物1 = 水樹奈々, entity=person, url), and let the Gallery with resourceRef show image+name. Hmm that duplicates name.

I think it's cleaner: Gallery with resourceRef for character; Gallery with resourceRef for person. Then text explaining entity types with the ids and names (names needed to explain identity distinction — that's arguably fine as it's the explanation content, minimal). I'll accept slight overlap since the explanation requires naming.

Actually let me reduce duplication: put the entity-type explanation in text using id + name (necessary for the identity distinction) and the images/links via the two Gallerys. That's reasonable.

Also note byte limits — fine.

2. Gallery: {title:"人物 1", resourceRef:"rr_84b73b5fea2541cee13dc37349e10b8b", items:[{personId:1}]}? Hmm the items schema for Gallery resourceRef variant allows personId/characterId keys. For resourceRef, items are "主键" selectors. I'll pass items: [{"personId":1}] and [{"characterId":1}].
